item.title: Ozone hole one of the largest in decades
item.description: In contrast to the 2025 seasonal ozone hole above Antarctica, which was the fifth smallest since 1992, this year's ozone hole ranks as one of the largest in 48 years, based on long-term atmospheric observations, including data from the Copernicus Sentinel-5P satellite. While this may sound alarming, it is important to remember that the size of the ozone hole varies naturally from year to year, and the long-term recovery of the ozone layer remains on track. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient skull reveals an early relative of the largest bone-cracking hyena
item.description: A newly identified prehistoric hyena from the northeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau aids in the quest to trace the origin of a lion-sized bone crusher. Its partial skull also records a remarkable recovery: The animal lost a canine tooth and survived long enough for bone to fill the socket. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
item.description: A Kenyan cult leader has been convicted of manslaughter over the deaths of 123 of his followers, having already been found guilty of murdering 191 others. Publicado también por: Sky News - World. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: France is dealing with water insecurity – a new study shows it's a global problem
item.description: Tens of thousands of people in France are living under water restrictions as the country deals with a drought despite recent rains, according to the environment ministry. But this is a global problem, as a new study released Wednesday revealed "the largest global decline in surface water resources recorded" since 1991, when data collection began. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Big EU defence projects under threat from proposed budget cuts: Commissioner Andrius Kubilius
item.description: We speak to the EU's Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andrius Kubilius. The former prime minister of Lithuania – who grew up during the Soviet era – tells us how he sees the confrontation between Europe and Russia. He also sounds the alarm over proposed cuts in the EU's future budget, saying that they could jeopardise major European projects in defence and space. Kubilius praises the EU's SAFE defence loans programme, remarking that it has been "really very successful". Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: From cyberbullying to extremist content, can EU Kids Act protect minors online?
item.description: Almost every European teenager is online. Some 96 percent of 15-year-olds use social media, yet many say they do not feel safe there. One in four children in the EU, aged 12 to 17, report having experienced cyberbullying, and nearly one in three say social media has left them feeling stressed, sad or socially excluded. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Why does the word 'huge' sound so large?
item.description: "Meow!" "Woof!" "Moo!" "Baa!" The words we use to describe animal sounds are clearly inspired by the actual sounds the animals make. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The dark matter puzzle deepens: Nearby galaxies challenge cosmic simulations
item.description: Galaxies appear to hold a surprise beneath their visible stars: Their inner regions contain less dark matter than some of our most advanced simulations predict. Dark matter is invisible, but its gravitational pull helps govern the motions of stars and gas. By measuring these movements, astronomers can reconstruct where this unseen matter lies and test the computer simulations used to understand the universe. A study of 136 nearby galaxies, involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), reveals a discrepancy that becomes more extensive in more massive systems, offering fresh clues… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights. In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated… Publicado también por: The Guardian - World, Al Jazeera English. item.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
item.description: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: Researchers reveal sex chromosome evolution and molecular sex markers in the pitcher plant Nepenthes mirabilis
item.description: Researchers have uncovered the genomic basis of sex determination in Nepenthes mirabilis, the only pitcher plant native to China, identifying an XX/XY sex chromosome system and molecular markers that can distinguish male from female plants long before they flower. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals perils of treating Putin like a corporate rival
item.description: Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars. During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Dolly Parton gets a deep-sea namesake: Bathyadmetella dollypartonae
item.description: A "beautiful" new species from one of the least-known areas of the ocean has been named after Dolly Parton. Scientists at the Natural History Museum work 9 to 5, and more besides, to name dozens of marine species every year. So, when they identified a new species of worm covered in pale, hairlike sheaths, there was only one choice for whom to name it after—and it wasn't Jolene. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: More than 57,000 granted UK permanent residence via BN(O) route in year to September
item.description: More than 57,000 arrivals from Hong Kong became permanent residents in the United Kingdom in the 12 months to September 2026 under the bespoke BN(O) immigration pathway launched five years ago, with the city ranking second behind India in the number of UK settlement grants during the period. According to the UK Home Office, 57,040 people were granted permanent residence via the BN(O) route in the 12 months to September 30, 2026. This was up from just 637 BN(O) grants in the preceding 12 months... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Turkey summons Georgian envoy after football fans' pro-Palestine protest sparks clashes
item.description: Turkey summoned ​Georgia's ambassador on ​Friday over violence that broke out ​at ‌a Europa ⁠League match in Batumi ‌between the Turkish Besiktas ⁠and Israeli Hapoel Beer-Sheva teams, according to a foreign ministry source. Clashes erupted after Besiktas fans unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the match, sparking the diplomatic row. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Sierra Leone: Maternal deaths fall as healthcare improves, but challenges remain
item.description: Sierra Leone was once considered one of the most dangerous countries in the world to give birth. Maternal deaths have since fallen dramatically, thanks to improvements in healthcare, medical training and maternity services. But despite this progress, significant challenges remain. Activists warn that continued efforts are needed to ensure safer pregnancies and childbirth for women across the country. Clarisse Fortuné reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: DR Congo: Copper reserves put Africa at the centre of the global race for critical minerals
item.description: Africa is emerging as a key player in the global race for copper, accounting for around 10 per cent of the world's estimated reserves. The Democratic Republic of Congo is at the centre of this growing interest, having mined 3.4 million metric tons of copper in 2025. Its vast mineral resources are attracting growing attention from countries and companies around the world, as demand for the metal rises due to its importance in energy infrastructure, electric vehicles and the global transition to cleaner energy. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Why Russia Is Erasing Stalin’s Crimes
item.description: Across Russia, memorials to victims of Joseph Stalin’s repressive regime are being quietly dismantled as more and more critics of the war in Ukraine are jailed. Our Moscow correspondent Valerie Hopkins takes us to one example of this erasure. Fuente: The New York Times - World.

item.title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
item.description: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez clinch an unlikely victory in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin DODMAN

item.title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
item.description: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Q&A: What matters most to homeowners facing flooding?
item.description: The annual amount of precipitation and the frequency of extreme events have increased in Pennsylvania in recent decades, and both are expected to continue increasing, leading to a higher flood risk. Most climate risk studies, however, reflect a limited understanding of how people interpret and act on flood risk. To develop a stronger culture of proactive disaster preparedness, that needs to change, according to Casey Helgeson, associate research professor in the Earth and Environmental Systems Institute at Penn State. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lizards build complex teeth differently from humans
item.description: Researchers from the Institute of Biotechnology, part of the Helsinki Institute of Life Science (HiLIFE) at the University of Helsinki, have shown how evolution can produce similarly complex tooth shapes through very different biological mechanisms. Fuente: Phys.org.
